why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 requires exit 1 and empty stdout, which is exactly what line 1 says. Check 2 requires `bad config:`, the exact path and line/column 3. Failing it for a "resolved or shortened" path follows from "exactly as passed". Check 3 requires `OK`, meaning it threw and the message contains the path. Check 4 requires `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and a deepEqual to `{port: 9000}`, all of which line 4 names. Check 5 requires `npm test` to pass at the head and at least one path-asserting test to fail against base `src/`, which matches "fails at the current base commit". The stricter items sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": reading the source to see whether line/column are computed, ENOENT handling, swallowing errors, and SyntaxError/cause. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond its expect line.
